label: Declared Node floors form five different values: @spec-kit/cli >=22.12.0; advisor ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0; spec-kit root/shared/runtime >=20.11.0; mcp-code-mode server >=24.0.0 <25.0.0 (hard, ABI 137); deep-loop/runtime and sk-doc >=20.11. The README single line 'Node.js 20.19+ (22.12+ for the spec-kit runtime CLI)' compresses them all; the operative floor for the first routed request (Code Mode MCP) is exactly Node 24.x.

README.md:162 'the advisor launcher installs and builds its own runtime on first run' is false. On a bare clone with no installs, node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs list-tools exits 1 with 'Cannot find module @spec-kit/shared/workspace/repo-root.mjs' (the shim loads the spec-kit CLI lib before any install), and the shim fails rather than builds on a missing/stale dist; dist-freshness.cjs contains no spawn/build path.

The step-2 -> step-3 dependency is real and unstated: running advisor npm install + run build BEFORE the spec-kit workspace install fails (exit 1) inside the build chain (npm --prefix ../../system-spec-kit/shared run build) with TS2591/TS2503 errors ('Cannot find name process', 'Cannot find namespace NodeJS'); the identical build exits 0 after step 2.

On Node 20.19.5 the floor mismatch is warn-only: npm 10.8.2 prints 'npm warn EBADENGINE Unsupported engine { package: @spec-kit/cli@1.7.2, required: >=22.12.0 }' and installs anyway (exit 0); advisor build, README verify list-tools, explicit workspace build and generate-context.js --help all exit 0 on 20.19.5. No Node-22-only API (node:sqlite, fs.globSync, process.loadEnvFile, process.getBuiltinModule) was found in CLI source.

The README verify command also exits 0 on Node 22.23.1 and 26.8.2. Node 18 is below every declared floor (all touched manifests are >=20.11 except the CLI at >=22.12) and was not installed on this machine, so its cell stays static.

Code Mode requires exactly Node 24.x: on a machine whose only interpreter is Node 26 (fake HOME, no version managers) the launcher prints '[mcp-code-mode-launcher] Cannot start the MCP server: no Node interpreter satisfies >=24.0.0 <25.0.0 (resolution reason: unsatisfied)' and exits 1. With nvm present it resolves a Node 24 interpreter and proceeds (then fails on the unbuilt clone server dist). So a single-Node 20/22/26 newcomer cannot start the MCP front door the README Verify step points at.

The documented README path leaves runtime/cli/dist absent, but validate.sh is designed for source-only checkouts: compiled orchestrator preferred, stale dist is a hard error with a rebuild instruction, and a missing dist falls back to running lib/validation/orchestrator.ts through the tsx loader (present after step 2). Not a Node-floor block.
